minutes.headline: Superintendent Burnham announced her retirement at year's end; a search subcommittee was formed
minutes.summary: The committee heard that Superintendent Burnham will retire at the end of the school year and appointed a search subcommittee; it also reviewed a restructured athletic-fee proposal, a Turkey Hill fire-alarm and door/security bid, a transportation contract renegotiation, and feedback on the joint town-building design plan's placement of the ACE program in a basement space. No final decisions were made on the fee schedule, cell-phone policy, or the building design; those were deferred to future meetings.

budget_items.what_was_said: Warrants for the period were reported to the committee for review.

budget_items.topic: Box Tops donation for field trips
budget_items.what_was_said: A donation was reported for acceptance to fund field trips.

budget_items.topic: Cultural Council donation for art supplies
budget_items.what_was_said: Remaining artist-in-residence money was donated for art supplies.
The PTO donated funds for STEM and reading materials.
A donor gave a scholarship award in memory of a former teacher.
The transportation bid initially came in with a large first-year increase before renegotiation.
The business office worked with the vendor to spread the increase more evenly across contract years.
Year-by-year increases across the 3-plus-2 year contract were read into the record.
A state grant payment took weeks to appear in the town's accounting system though it had already arrived.
The choice revolving account has been used to cover unbudgeted bills; its buffer is described as thin.
The registrar has been invoicing renters of school facilities; most invoiced amounts had not yet been collected.
The Munis-recorded balance for the facilities revolving account lags behind actual deposits.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill fire alarm upgrade bid
budget_items.what_was_said: The lowest bid for the fire alarm/voice evacuation upgrade came in above expectations due to a new code requirement.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funds applied to Turkey Hill fire alarm gap
budget_items.what_was_said: The town released ARPA funding to close the funding gap on the fire alarm project.
The full bid for door replacement and security across all doors came in well above available capital.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill door project, available capital
budget_items.what_was_said: Only enough capital remains to fund a phase-one scope of the doors and security system.
Coaching stipends rose this year and are set to rise again next year, pressuring the athletic budget.
The full amount reserved in the local budget for athletics was spent.
User fees and gate receipts make up the revenue side of the athletic revolving account.
The revolving account funds officials, an athletics secretary, and coaching stipends, exceeding revenue coming in.

budget_items.topic: total athletic budget and fee share
budget_items.what_was_said: User fees were said to cover roughly a quarter of the total combined athletic budget.

budget_items.topic: athletic fee projection at full pay
budget_items.what_was_said: A projection assuming every participant paid full price was run against FY24 participation.
A new per-season fee was proposed for high school and middle school, with sibling, reduced, and waiver tiers and a family cap.
Neighboring towns' average per-season fees were used as a benchmark for the proposal.

budget_items.topic: athletic fee revenue target to hold 26% share
budget_items.what_was_said: To keep user fees at the same share of a rising athletic budget, more revenue would need to come in next year.
FinCom reported the town's free cash figure for the year, ahead of budget season.

budget_items.topic: state funding growth vs. district cost growth (resolutions draft)
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member argued the state's funding share is growing much slower than district costs, motivating a legislative resolution.

decisions.decision: Wait for the January 21 MSBA superintendents' webinar before deciding whether to file a statement of interest for the remaining Turkey Hill door replacement.

The department will formally provide the design committee written feedback objecting to placing the ACE program's special education students in the lower-level/basement space of the proposed municipal building.
Proceed with a phase-one door/security award (not to exceed $300,000) at Turkey Hill, deferring full door replacement pending MSBA information.
The HR director will no longer serve as the second voting member on the Sick Bank committee; a committee member will serve instead.
Take no formal vote on the restructured athletic fee proposal tonight; gather public/booster feedback before a decision closer to the FY budget vote.
Bring the cell phone use discussion back at a future meeting (next meeting or first meeting in February) with feedback from a regional legislative conversation.
Revise the draft school committee resolutions document to be shorter and less numerically dense before it comes back for further discussion.

what_happened.line: Superintendent Burnham announced her retirement at the end of the school year, and the committee appointed a two-member search subcommittee.
The committee took no vote on a restructured athletic fee proposal, choosing to gather public and booster feedback before deciding nearer the budget vote.
Dr. Gilson was authorized to negotiate and finalize a renegotiated transportation contract after an initial bid came in with a steep first-year increase.
The department will send the town's building design committee written objection to placing the ACE special education program in a basement-level space.
A phase-one door and security award was approved at Turkey Hill, with full door replacement deferred pending state (MSBA) guidance.

why_it_matters: A superintendent search will shape district leadership heading into next school year, and residents will see subcommittee updates as it proceeds.
The undecided athletic fee proposal will factor into the FY budget residents vote on, once public and booster feedback is gathered.
Where the ACE special education program is housed in the planned joint municipal building affects students and families relying on that program.
